state.misconception_label: Struggles to visualise nets of 3D shapes

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: This is the net of a... ![A circle touching a sector](). I got Triangle because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let's focus on identifying the overall shape of the net first. Remember, the net should represent all the faces of the 3D shape when unfolded. Can you walk me through how you approached this net?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I guess I just looked at the shapes and thought about what they could make. I saw the circle and the curved part, but I'm not sure how they fit together. Could it be something like a cone? I'm really confused about how to tell the difference between all the shapes!

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let's focus on identifying the net components one at a time. Remember, each shape on the net represents a face of the 3D shape when unfolded. Can you think about how the circle and curved part could fit together to form a 3D shape? This process involves visualizing how the 2D net transforms into a 3D shape, similar to how we've discussed in previous examples.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I think I get what you're saying about the circle and the curved part fitting together. So, if it is a cone, the circle would be the base, right? But I still don't really understand how to picture it all coming together. How do I know for sure it's a cone and not something else?

score.justification_pass1: The teacher repeatedly asks generic questions about 'identifying components' and 'visualizing' without providing concrete strategies to help the student actually visualize the net folding into a cone, leaving the student still confused by Turn 4.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher uses guided questioning and asks the student to walk through their thinking rather than directly explaining with worked examples, which contradicts the core traditional approach of explicit instruction.
